triage.note: Intel FY2024 (filed 2025-01-31, intc-20241228.htm). The filing states in its own words that it is not arranged like a conventional 10-K: the body is a business narrative and the ONLY `Item N.` headings in the whole document sit in a `Form 10-K Cross-Reference Index` at normalized_text offset 514,332 of 517,976 — the last 0.7% of the file. The segmenter does exactly the right thing with that (those ARE the headings, so those ARE the spans) and the result is 23 items covering 0.3% of the document, which `low_item_coverage` already reported and `doc_status: ambiguous` already refused to call success. THIS CASE ASSERTS THE OTHER HALF: that the index's own page references resolve. WHY THE SPANS DO NOT MOVE, and this is the load-bearing part — Intel's page ranges OVERLAP and NEST. Item 3 (Legal Proceedings) is pages 102-105, inside item 8's 56-108, because Intel answers it in Note 19 to the financial statements; item 2 (Properties) is pages 11 and 32, inside item 1's 3-24; item 7's 18-29 overlaps item 1's 3-24 because one narrative serves both. No assignment of those ranges to `start`/`end` can satisfy INV-S1, so the resolved regions travel as `evidence.cross_reference` — the shape ADR-031 already chose for the footnote case, for the same reason. doc_status STAYS `ambiguous` and `low_item_coverage` STAYS fired: the primary spans really are index entries, and softening either would be the dishonest half of this fix. WHAT THE PAID TIER DID ON THIS EXACT FILING, for contrast: ADR-036 §k records two attempts, the second billed $0.997760, both returning `empty_completion`, zero items resolved. The deterministic resolution here answers all 13 resolvable items at $0, so ADR-042 §e suppresses the escalation trigger on a filing whose index resolved — the one measured case where a paid rung is known to fail. EXCLUSION ANCHOR, CORRECTED IN THE OPEN: the frozen prediction named 'Form 10-K Cross-Reference Index' as the string that must not appear inside a resolved region, and that assertion FAILED on item 8 — not because the resolution reached the index, which `resolve` structurally forbids (every region is clipped at `index_start`), but because Intel prints a mini table of contents at the head of the financial-statements section, at offset 291,363, that lists the index among the sections and names it. The phrase occurs four times in the filing and only the fourth is the index itself. The anchor is now 'Item Number Item', the index's own column header, which occurs exactly once in the document. The original anchor was a bad instrument, not a finding about the fix, and it is recorded here rather than quietly swapped.
